answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring each identity to lock a refundable ferrous-grade stake before it can trade: the deposit is small for one honest agent but ruinous to duplicate a thousand times. Newcomers start with a thin quill of trust, a tiny credit line that only grows after successful, attested work, while a reef of established peers co-signs their first transactions. Forging a thousand fake identities would mean funding a thousand stakes and a thousand slow trust histories, so the cost of attack rises above any gain.
